evidence.title: Downtown Grand Forks
evidence.text: Downtown Grand Forks is the original commercial center of Grand Forks, North Dakota.

evidence.title: Downtown Grand Forks
evidence.text: Located on the western bank of the Red River of the North, the downtown neighborhood is situated near the fork of the Red River and the Red Lake River.

evidence.title: Downtown Grand Forks
evidence.text: While downtown is no longer the dominant commercial area of the Greater Grand Forks community, it remains the historic center of Grand Forks.

evidence.title: Downtown Grand Forks
evidence.text: An 80.4 acre portion was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2005, as Downtown Grand Forks Historic District.

evidence.title: Downtown Grand Forks
evidence.text: Today, downtown Grand Forks is home to many offices, stores, restaurants, and bars.

evidence.title: Red Lake River
evidence.text: The Red Lake River (French: "Rivière du Lac Rouge"; Ojibwe: "Miskwaagamiiwi-zaaga'iganiiwi-ziibi") is a river located in northwestern Minnesota.

evidence.title: Red Lake River
evidence.text: The river begins on the western side of the Lower Red Lake and flows westward.

evidence.title: Red Lake River
evidence.text: After passing through Thief River Falls, Red Lake Falls, and Crookston, the river merges with the Red River of the North in East Grand Forks.

evidence.title: Red Lake River
evidence.text: The total length of the river is 193 miles (310.6 km).

evidence.title: Red Lake River
evidence.text: The term "Forks" in Grand Forks comes from this forking (confluence) of the Red and Red Lake rivers near downtown Grand Forks.

evidence.title: Grand Forks International
evidence.text: The Grand Forks International (GFI) is an annual international invitational baseball tournament hosted at James Donaldson Park in Grand Forks, British Columbia.

evidence.title: Grand Forks International
evidence.text: The GFI is the largest invitational baseball tournament in Canada and is a large part of the culture in Grand Forks.

evidence.title: Grand Forks International
evidence.text: The tournament is also notable for being run entirely by volunteers.

evidence.title: Grand Sky
evidence.text: Grand Sky is an UAS (unmanned aerial systems)-specific business and aviation park located at Grand Forks Air Force Base near Grand Forks, North Dakota.

evidence.title: Grand Sky
evidence.text: A groundbreaking for the development was held in September 2015, making it the first UAS business and aviation park in the U.S.

evidence.title: Grand Sky
evidence.text: The park consists of 217 acres and includes access to the Grand Forks Air Force Base runway for large UAS flights.

evidence.title: Grand Forks Municipal Airport
evidence.text: Grand Forks Municipal Airport is a former airport, located within current city limits approximately 3 mi west-northwest of central Grand Forks, North Dakota.

evidence.title: Grand Forks Municipal Airport
evidence.text: It was closed shortly after World War II and is now redeveloped as part of the urban area of Grand Forks.

evidence.title: Grand Forks International Airport
evidence.text: Grand Forks International Airport (IATA: GFK, ICAO: KGFK, FAA LID: GFK) is a public airport five miles (8 km) northwest of Grand Forks, in Grand Forks County, North Dakota.

evidence.title: Grand Forks International Airport
evidence.text: GFK has no scheduled passenger flights out of the country but has an "international" title (like many other airports) because it has customs service for arrivals from Canada and other countries.
